source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Reassess distal circulation, sensation, and movement after the splint is applied and act promptly if neurovascular status worsens.","B":"Tighten the splint until distal pulses become difficult to palpate so movement of the suspected fracture is minimized during transport.","C":"Remove and reapply the splint repeatedly during transport to test movement at the injured area and confirm alignment.","D":"Ignore new numbness or tingling when external alignment is preserved because sensory changes are expected after immobilization."}}
source_row.rationale: StatPearls states that neurovascular status must be assessed before and after splint placement and that changes after splinting should prompt rapid splint removal and reassessment.

source_row.stem: A nurse is immobilizing a suspected forearm fracture before transport. Which action is essential after applying the splint?
